title: Making Negative Statements and Commands
summary: Make present, past and future statements negative using the correct auxiliary. Use not with be and modal verbs, and use do, does or did where a simple verb needs a negative form.
learningObjectives: Make negative sentences with present and past forms of be.
Use not with have, has, will, can and other auxiliary or modal verbs.
Use don’t, doesn’t and didn’t before the base form of a main verb.
Form negative commands with don’t plus the base form.

explanation.heading: Put not after a form of be
explanation.body: With am, is, are, was and were, put not immediately after the verb. In everyday speech, many negative forms have contractions: isn’t, aren’t, wasn’t and weren’t. For I am not, the usual short form is I’m not, not I amn’t.
explanation.example: The cafés weren’t open when we arrived.

explanation.heading: Negate an auxiliary or modal directly
explanation.body: Add not after an auxiliary such as have or has, or after a modal such as can, could, will, would, must or should. Common contractions include haven’t, hasn’t, can’t, couldn’t, won’t, wouldn’t, mustn’t and shouldn’t. The negative of will is won’t, not willn’t.
explanation.example: I haven’t packed my bag, and I won’t leave without it.

explanation.heading: Use do, does or did with simple verbs
explanation.body: When an ordinary present-simple or past-simple verb has no auxiliary, make it negative with do not, does not or did not. Use don’t with I, we, you and they; doesn’t with he, she and it; and didn’t with any subject for the past simple.
explanation.example: My neighbours don’t own a car, and Rosa doesn’t drive.

explanation.heading: Keep the main verb in its base form
explanation.body: After don’t, doesn’t or didn’t, use the base form of the main verb, without an -s or past ending. This still applies when do itself is the main verb: doesn’t do and didn’t do are correct patterns.
explanation.example: Eli didn’t buy any bread on the way home.

explanation.heading: Make a negative command with don’t
explanation.body: To tell someone not to do something, begin the command with Don’t and use the base form of the verb. Do not add to between don’t and the verb.
explanation.example: Don’t leave the window open overnight.

left.label: Be or an existing auxiliary
left.note: Add not to is; no extra do is needed.

right.label: Present simple main verb
right.example: The shop doesn’t open on Mondays.
right.note: Use doesn’t before the base form open.

left.label: Present simple
left.note: Doesn’t matches the third-person singular subject.

right.label: Past simple
right.note: Didn’t marks the past; cook stays in its base form.

examples.sentence: My shoes aren’t dry, so I’ll wear a different pair.
examples.note: Aren’t is the negative of are.

examples.sentence: We weren’t at the station at eight.
examples.note: Weren’t makes past be negative with a plural subject.

examples.sentence: Sam hasn’t answered my email yet.
examples.note: Hasn’t makes the present perfect negative.

examples.sentence: The baby doesn’t sleep in this room.
examples.note: Doesn’t is followed by the base form sleep.

examples.sentence: Please don’t put your coat on the wet bench.

commonMistakes.why: The usual contracted negative with I am is I’m not.
After doesn’t, the main verb must be in its base form.

commonMistakes.incorrect: They didn’t went to the market.
commonMistakes.correct: They didn’t go to the market.
commonMistakes.why: Didn’t already marks the past, so use go, not went.
A negative command uses don’t followed directly by the base verb.

studyTips: Look for be, have or a modal before adding do: these verbs can take not directly.
When you write doesn’t or didn’t, check that the main verb has no -s or past ending.
Practise negative commands as one pattern: Don’t + base verb.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct negative verb: “We ___ ready to leave yet.”
exercises.feedback: We takes are, so the negative form is aren’t.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct negative auxiliary: “Nadia ___ finished her homework yet.”
exercises.feedback: Finished is a past participle in the present perfect, so use hasn’t.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct negative form: “Our guests ___ be here tonight; they arrive tomorrow.”
exercises.feedback: Won’t is will not; it correctly forms the negative future expression won’t be.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct negative verb: “Yesterday, Mateo ___ bring his lunch.”
exercises.feedback: Yesterday refers to the past, so use didn’t before the base verb bring.

exercises.prompt: My parents ___ at home last night. They stayed at a hotel. Use a contraction of were not.
exercises.feedback: Weren’t is the contracted negative of were, the past form of be for my parents.

exercises.prompt: Felix ___ got a bicycle. He walks everywhere. Use a contraction of has not.
exercises.feedback: Hasn’t got expresses that Felix does not have a bicycle.

exercises.prompt: Tina ___ eat meat. She chooses vegetarian dishes. Use a contraction of does not.
exercises.feedback: Doesn’t is the present-simple negative for Tina; eat stays in its base form.

exercises.prompt: We ___ go to the beach last Sunday because it rained. Use a contraction of did not.
exercises.feedback: Didn’t makes the past-simple sentence negative, and go remains in its base form.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: “The children wasn’t hungry after school.”
acceptedAnswers: The children weren’t hungry after school.
The children were not hungry after school.
exercises.feedback: The plural subject the children needs weren’t, not wasn’t.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: “Ruby doesn’t likes orange juice.”
acceptedAnswers: Ruby does not like orange juice.
exercises.feedback: After doesn’t, remove the -s ending from like.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: “I didn’t did the washing yesterday.”
acceptedAnswers: I didn’t do the washing yesterday.
I did not do the washing yesterday.
exercises.feedback: After didn’t, use the base verb do, even when the main verb is do.

exercises.prompt: Correct the command: “Don’t to touch the hot pan.”
acceptedAnswers: Do not touch the hot pan.
exercises.feedback: Don’t is followed immediately by the base form touch, without to.

speakingExercises.prompt: Turn “I am tired” into a negative sentence. Use the contraction I’m not and say the full sentence.
speakingExercises.feedback: For I am, the natural contracted negative is I’m not.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make this statement negative and say the full sentence: “Maya plays the piano.” Use doesn’t.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use doesn’t with Maya and keep play in its base form.

speakingExercises.prompt: Give the negative command for “Close the door.” Say one complete sentence using don’t.
speakingExercises.feedback: A negative command begins with don’t followed by the base verb close.

speakingExercises.prompt: Every morning, Nora drinks tea, but she never drinks coffee. Say one sentence about her coffee habit using doesn't or does not.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use doesn't + the base verb drink for a third-person singular present-simple negative.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change 'The visitors entered the gallery yesterday' into a negative sentence. Keep all the facts and use didn't or did not.
acceptedAnswers: The visitors didn't enter the gallery yesterday.
The visitors did not enter the gallery yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: After didn't, use the base verb enter, not the past form entered.

speakingExercises.prompt: Someone asks, 'Are the windows clean?' They are not clean. Reply with a full sentence starting 'No, they' and ending with 'clean'.
speakingExercises.feedback: With the plural subject they, negate are using aren't, they're not, or are not.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the grammar in 'The workers hasn't finished yet.' Say the whole corrected sentence without changing its meaning.
acceptedAnswers: The workers have not finished yet.
speakingExercises.feedback: Workers is plural, so the negative present-perfect auxiliary is haven't, not hasn't.

speakingExercises.prompt: The oven handle is hot and unsafe. Tell a friend not to touch the handle, then say it is not safe. Use two short sentences, beginning 'Don't' and 'It'.
acceptedAnswers: Don't touch the handle. It isn't safe.
Don't touch the handle. It's not safe.
Don't touch the handle. It is not safe.
speakingExercises.feedback: Don't + base verb gives a negative command; it isn't / it's not / it is not describes the danger.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children were sleepy after lunch.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which sentence is the correct negative version of the statement you hear?
choices: The children wasn’t sleepy after lunch.
The children weren’t sleepy after lunch.
The children didn’t sleepy after lunch.
listeningExercises.feedback: Were becomes weren’t in a negative sentence; did not is not used with the adjective sleepy.

listeningExercises.audioText: My uncle drove to work this morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly makes the statement you hear negative?
choices: My uncle doesn’t drove to work this morning.
My uncle wasn’t drive to work this morning.
My uncle didn’t drive to work this morning.
listeningExercises.feedback: The past-simple negative is didn’t plus the base verb drive.

listeningExercises.audioText: You shouldn’t leave your bicycle here.
listeningExercises.prompt: Listen and type only the negative modal immediately before the verb leave.
listeningExercises.feedback: Shouldn’t is the negative contraction of should not.

listeningExercises.audioText: Amina isn't at the market today. She's at home because she's feeling ill.
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker says Amina isn't at the market and explains that she is at home.

listeningExercises.audioText: The team didn't finish the bridge repairs on Tuesday, but they finished them on Wednesday morning.
listeningExercises.feedback: Didn't finish rules out Tuesday; finished on Wednesday morning tells us when the work ended.

listeningExercises.audioText: The manager hasn't approved the booking yet, but she won't cancel it.
listeningExercises.prompt: What is true about the booking right now?
choices: It is still waiting for approval.
listeningExercises.feedback: Hasn't approved ... yet describes an unfinished approval. Won't cancel describes a different future action.

listeningExercises.audioText: Ben couldn't reach the station this morning because the road was closed.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the contracted negative modal immediately after the person's name.
listeningExercises.feedback: Couldn't is the contraction of could not and expresses an inability in the past.

listeningExercises.audioText: Please don't move the chairs until the floor is dry.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word negative instruction between 'Please' and 'the chairs'.
listeningExercises.feedback: Don't move uses don't + base verb to give a negative instruction.
